stem: An adult admitted to an acute-care hospital is known to be colonized with vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE). Which transmission-based approach is most appropriate under CDC MDRO guidance?

options.A: Use Standard Precautions plus Contact Precautions for the known target-MDRO colonization according to the hospital's infection-control program
options.B: Use Airborne Precautions because VRE is primarily transmitted through airborne droplet nuclei
options.C: Use no precautions because colonization cannot contribute to healthcare transmission
options.D: Use Droplet Precautions alone and omit Standard Precautions

rationale: CDC MDRO guidance for acute-care hospitals recommends routine Contact Precautions for patients infected with target MDROs and for patients previously identified as colonized, while Standard Precautions remain foundational. VRE is transmitted mainly through direct or indirect contact, including contaminated environmental surfaces and equipment, not through the airborne route.
educational_objective: Apply setting-specific CDC precautions for known VRE colonization in an acute-care hospital.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_document_title: Management of Multidrug-Resistant Organisms in Healthcare Settings — Summary of Recommendations
source_version_date: CDC web update March–April 2024; current guidance accessed 2026
source_locator: V.A.5.c.i Acute-care hospitals — implement Contact Precautions routinely for patients infected with target MDROs and known colonized patients; Standard Precautions remain required
source_claim_supported: In acute-care hospitals, known colonization with a target MDRO such as VRE calls for Contact Precautions in addition to Standard Precautions under CDC guidance.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based precautions and infection prevention
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — VRE/MDRO precautions
correction_summary: Added the acute-care setting to eliminate a real ambiguity: CDC recommendations differ in LTC and ambulatory settings. Clarified that Contact Precautions supplement rather than replace Standard Precautions.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Acute-care Contact Precautions and continued Standard Precautions are supported.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; colonization can contribute to transmission.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect route and omission of Standard Precautions.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A matches the specified acute-care setting.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked acute care versus LTC/ambulatory differences, colonization versus infection and facility-target MDRO definitions; setting is now explicit.
